text.p: Here are highlights of stories in Romania's press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy:
Business:
BURSA
- The government is expected to complete drafting of the 1997 state budget early in February.
ROMANIA LIBERA
- The U.S. State Department will give Romania $6.5 million to buy defence equipment for its Partnership for Peace participation, the Foreign Ministry said.

- The general police inspectorate opened investigations into alleged complicity to fraud by Alexandru Dinulescu, president of Bankcoop SA commercial bank, the newspaper quotes a police department as saying.
- Romania raised its contribution to the capital of the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development by 48 million Ecus ($56 million).
- The presidency replaced its five members on the board of the State Ownership Fund (FPS).
- Banca Romana de Comert Exterior Bancorex SA increased its interest rates on deposits by up to 12 percentage points.
ADEVARUL
- Train fares are expected to rise by around 140 percent in February at the earliest.
AZI
- The FPS rejects accusations in a Court of Accounts report saying the capital of some of the companies privatised so far had been undervalued.
- Citibank opened its first subsidiary in Romania promising to help finance infrastructure projects.
ZIUA
- Rom Telecom RA telephone company plans to increase telephone charges by 80 percent.
LIBERTATEA
- The National Privatisation Agency worked out a draft programme on privatisation over 1997-2000.
EVENIMENTUL ZILEI
- Agriculture Minister Dinu Gavrilescu said disadvantaged farmers would get loans to smooth the effects of recent and expected price rises.
CRONICA ROMANA
- The National Oil Company said it expected to sign a contract with Chase Manhattan Bank on a syndicated loan to finance oil imports.
General:
ROAMNIA LIBERA
- Ex-president Ion Iliescu, leader of the opposition Party of Social Democracy, threatened to launch a no-confidence motion against new centrist government.
- Foreign Minister Adrian Severin promotes the idea of simultaneous admission of all ex-Warsaw Pact members into NATO.
COTIDIANUL
- President Emil Constantinescu continued a series of talks with leaders of opposition parties on Romania's present eeconomic and social situation.
- Lawyers hired by miners' leader Miron Cosma, detained over his role in violent riots in 1991, said they would not defend Cosma in court.
- United States government will donate $100,000 for Romania's street children.
CURIERUL NATIONAL
- Improper storage conditions put in jeopardy scores of books owned by the National Library.
- British Foreign Secretary Malcolm Rifkind praised Romania's democratic progress during a visit to Bucharest.
ADEVARUL
- More than 230,000 Romanians left the country over the past six months due to poor living standards here.
CRONICA ROMANA
- Romania will launch a stratgic partnership with Poland and Hungary as part of its plans to integrate in NATO, Foreign Minister Adrian Severin is quoted as saying.
EVENIMENTUL ZILEI
- Interview with Justice Minister Gavril Dejeu on miners' riots in 1990 and preferential credits given by Bancorex SA bank to interior ministry staff.
-- Bucharest newsroom 40-1 3120264
